ledger.x: 958: Boso I is the first count of La Marche.
1308: the childless Count Guy dies and the crown seizes the county.
1314: the king makes La Marche an appanage for his youngest son.
1327: La Marche passes to the House of Bourbon.
1435: the House of Armagnac takes La Marche.
1477: Louis XI confiscates the lands of Jacques d'Armagnac and La Marche reverts to the Bourbons.
1527: Francis I seizes La Marche and it becomes crown domain.

certainty.note: The page says the county's area 'was increased during the 13th century, after which, however, it remained unaltered'; no boundary record is given.
